group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A previously healthy-appearing 33-year-old man arrived by rideshare to the emergency department in the late morning of an early autumn weekday, reporting that over the preceding thirty-six hours he had developed shaking chills followed by a dry cough that transformed overnight into a productive one yielding small streaks of rusty sputum; he also noted pleuritic discomfort along his right mid-axillary line whenever he tried to inhale deeply, prompting shallow, rapid breaths that left him feeling “winded even when just seated.” He works as a bicycle courier, lives alone in a downtown studio apartment, cycles daily without difficulty, and performs all activities of daily living independently; he specifically denied any recent health-care facility stay or chronic institutional care. Review of past medical history revealed a remote viral myocarditis in early adolescence that led to a persistently reduced ejection fraction of 35 % for which he follows cardiology and takes carvedilol 25 mg twice daily and a modest dose of sacubitril-valsartan, along with furosemide 20 mg most mornings. A separate hepatology clinic monitors him for biopsy-proven autoimmune hepatitis with early bridging fibrosis; laboratory surveillance six months earlier showed normal albumin and INR, and he has never required lactulose, diuretics for ascites, or endoscopic variceal therapy. He volunteered that no clinician has ever informed him of kidney trouble, stroke, transient ischemic attack, or malignancy, and he last saw his primary physician three months ago for an employment physical that was “completely normal.” He quit cigarette smoking five years ago after totaling roughly seven pack-years, drinks an occasional craft beer after weekend shifts, and denies illicit substance use. He had taken no over-the-counter antipyretics, inhalers, antibiotics, or supplemental oxygen before arrival; the only medication ingested this morning was his usual carvedilol with a glass of water. At triage he sat upright but leaned forward with elbows on the knees, speaking between gasps yet fully oriented to person, place, date, and current events. Skin was warm and dry, mucous membranes appeared tacky, and capillary refill was brisk. Pre-intervention vital signs documented an oral temperature of 99.1 °F, a markedly tachycardic pulse of 132 beats min⁻¹ that was regular, non-invasive blood pressure 147/82 mm Hg (systolic manually confirmed), an extraordinarily rapid respiratory rate of 53 breaths min⁻¹ with visible alae nasi flaring and mild intercostal indrawing, and fingertip pulse oximetry fluctuating between 92 % and 94 % while breathing ambient air at sea-level altitude. Neck veins sat 4 cm above the sternal angle, consistent with his baseline cardiology documentation, and trace symmetric ankle edema was again observed. Cardiac auscultation revealed a rapid S1 and S2 with a soft third sound but no new murmurs or rub. Pulmonary examination demonstrated coarse inspiratory crackles throughout the right lower posterior lung without dullness to percussion, and vesicular breath sounds elsewhere; no wheezes were heard. Abdominal palpation disclosed a smooth liver edge one centimeter below the costal margin, nontender, with no splenomegaly or distension. A screening neurologic assessment showed equal, reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, fluent speech, and 5/5 motor strength in all extremities. A bedside glucometer read 97 mg dL⁻¹ prior to intravenous cannulation. Venous samples and a right radial arterial puncture were obtained within ten minutes of arrival before any crystalloid flushes beyond the small heparin lock were administered. Basic metabolic panel returned a profoundly elevated sodium level of 160 mEq L⁻¹, potassium 3.8 mEq L⁻¹, chloride 104 mEq L⁻¹, bicarbonate 24 mEq L⁻¹, blood urea nitrogen 58 mg dL⁻¹, and creatinine 1.1 mg dL⁻¹—above his recent baseline for urea despite creatinine remaining in the normal range, suggestive of hypovolemic concentration rather than intrinsic nephropathy. Complete blood count revealed leukocytosis to 15.4 × 10⁹ L⁻¹ with neutrophil predominance, hematocrit 42 %, hemoglobin 14.0 g dL⁻¹, and platelets 238 × 10⁹ L⁻¹. An arterial blood gas on room air demonstrated an alkalemic pH of 7.67, PaCO₂ 27 mm Hg, PaO₂ 97 mm Hg, calculated bicarbonate 24 mEq L⁻¹, and a base excess of +3, consistent with primary respiratory alkalosis attributed to pain-induced hyperventilation. Serum lactate measured 1.7 mmol L⁻¹. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph, obtained before any medication or fluid therapy, displayed a homogeneous consolidation occupying the right lower lobe with air bronchograms and preserved costophrenic angles; no fluid meniscus, no contralateral infiltrate, and no mediastinal shift were seen. Electrocardiography performed simultaneously showed sinus tachycardia at 133 beats min⁻¹ with nonspecific ST-T flattening identical to prior outpatient tracings. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, an expectorated sputum sample for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Legionella and Streptococcus pneumoniae, and a multiplex respiratory viral panel were dispatched to the laboratory before any antimicrobial, antipyretic, bronchodilator, vasoactive, or diuretic agents were ordered. At the moment of this documentation the patient remains seated upright on the gurney breathing room air, receiving no intravenous fluids or oxygen, thereby preserving the physiologic observations and laboratory data above as his untreated presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI), using pretreatment findings:
- Demographics: a man's age contributes one point per year, so age 33 gives 33. No nursing-home residence (+10 if present): 0.
- Comorbidities: chronic liver disease from biopsy-proven autoimmune hepatitis (+20) and heart failure with EF 35% (+10) contribute 30. No malignancy (+30), cerebrovascular disease (+10), or chronic renal disease (+10): 0 each.
- Examination: respiratory rate 53/min meets the ≥30 threshold (+20); pulse 132/min meets the ≥125 threshold (+10). He is oriented, systolic BP is 147 mmHg, and temperature is 99.1°F, so altered mental status (+20), systolic BP <90 (+20), and temperature <35°C or ≥40°C (+15) each score 0. Examination subtotal: 30.
- Tests: BUN 58 mg/dL meets the ≥30 threshold (+20). Arterial pH 7.67 is not <7.35 (+30); sodium 160 is not <130 mEq/L (+20); glucose 97 is not ≥250 mg/dL (+10); hematocrit 42% is not <30% (+10); room-air PaO₂ 97 is not <60 mmHg (+10); and there is no pleural effusion (+10). Each of these remaining criteria scores 0.
Sum: 33 + 30 + 30 + 20 = 113 (PSI class IV).
Final answer: 113
